short: BCL6 and its paralogue BCL6B (BAZF) are BTB/POZ zinc-finger repressors that bind a nine-base site, TTCCTAGAA, which is a TTCNNNGAA element of the same class that STAT dimers use. That overlap is not incidental: BCL6 represses interleukin-4-induced, STAT6-dependent genes by occupying sites that STAT6 would otherwise use, so the same sequence can be an activating STAT element or a repressed BCL6 element depending on which protein is present. BCL6 is required for germinal center formation and for follicular helper T cells, and its deregulation by chromosomal translocation or promoter mutation occurs in a large fraction of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. A hit to this motif is ambiguous between BCL6, BCL6B and the STAT family.
long:
## The factors

Two paralogues: BCL6 (also LAZ3, ZBTB27) and BCL6B (BAZF, ZBTB28). Both have the standard BTB-ZF architecture - an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain, a central region with PEST and RD2 repression motifs, and six C-terminal C2H2 zinc fingers [PMID:8692924]. The BTB domain obligately homodimerizes, and the dimer creates a lateral groove at the interface into which the SMRT and NCOR corepressors dock through a short peptide; the crystal structure of that complex explained how one BTB dimer recruits corepressor and provided the target site for the small-molecule BCL6 inhibitors and degraders developed since [PMID:14690607]. Repression is therefore corepressor-dependent and also involves BCOR and HDAC recruitment. BCL6 is expressed at high levels in germinal center B cells and in follicular helper T cells, at lower levels in macrophages and other tissues [PMID:9171827,19628815]; BCL6B is expressed in endothelium, some T-cell subsets and neural tissue and is much less studied. The two proteins bind DNA as dimers, and the six fingers give a footprint consistent with a nine- to twelve-base site.

## The motif

The site is written in the literature as TTCCTAGAA, sometimes generalized to TTCCT(A/C)GAA [PMID:7945383,11374866]. Parsed as TTC-CTA-GAA it is a TTCNNNGAA element - structurally the same family of sites that STAT dimers occupy as gamma-interferon activated sequences (GAS elements) [PMID:9110977,11374866]. All the matrices here are consistent with that once strand is taken into account: the HOCOMOCO grade-A BCL6 model reads GCTTTCGAGGAAT and JASPAR MA0463.3 reads GCTTTCGAGGAA, whose reverse complements are TTCCTCGAAAGC, while the BCL6B HT-SELEX models read TGCTTTCTAGGAATTCA, reverse-complementing to TTCCTAGAAAGCA [PMID:23332764]. So BCL6 models favor TTCCTCGAA and BCL6B models TTCCTAGAA; both fit TTCCTNGAA, and the difference at that one central position is the only sequence feature that even hints at a paralogue distinction. It is not enough to act on: the BCL6 and BCL6B models are 0.91-0.97 similar, and the Vierstra archetype for the family is named AC0665:BCL/BCL6B, an explicit statement that the two were not separable. Information content is high for a C2H2 family - the BCL6B matrices reach nearly 30 bits because they include long flanks - but much of that comes from the flanking bases selected in vitro rather than from the core, and long high-information matrices of this kind tend to overfit. One entry in the family contradicts the rest outright: CIS-BP M00227, labelled BCL6, reads TAATTAA and its nearest cross-database neighbors are PRD-like homeodomain motifs. It does not belong with the other BCL6 models.

## Where it acts

BCL6 binds promoters and enhancers of genes that must be held off during the germinal center reaction: DNA damage response and checkpoint genes (TP53, CDKN1A, ATR), differentiation genes (PRDM1), and cytokine and chemokine genes [PMID:21900183,22894929]. In T cells it represses the Th1, Th2 and Th17 programs while promoting the follicular helper program [PMID:19628815]. Because the site is a GAS-type element, BCL6 sites overlap physically with STAT sites at shared loci - the germline immunoglobulin epsilon (Iepsilon) promoter is the worked example, where BCL6 occupancy blocks STAT6-driven transcription and IgE class switching [PMID:10490661]. TTCCTNGAA is AT-rich, CpG-free and about nine informative bases, so chance occurrences are frequent; occupancy is set by BCL6 abundance, which is itself tightly controlled by phosphorylation-triggered degradation and by MYC-driven transcription in the germinal center.

## Biology and disease

Bcl6-null mice form no germinal centers, cannot mount high-affinity antibody responses, and develop a lethal inflammatory syndrome with eosinophilia and Th2-skewed cytokine production [PMID:9110977,9171827] - a phenotype that connects directly to the STAT6 antagonism. Bcl6 is also required for follicular helper T cell development, and enforced Bcl6 expression drives T cells into that program [PMID:19628815]. In human disease, BCL6 is the most frequently translocated locus in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: chromosomal rearrangements juxtapose heterologous promoters to the BCL6 coding sequence and prevent its normal downregulation [PMID:8235596], and point mutations in the BCL6 promoter region have the same effect. BCL6 is also deregulated in follicular lymphoma and in some T-cell lymphomas. The BTB lateral groove has been exploited pharmacologically, with peptide and small-molecule inhibitors and BTB-directed degraders in development [PMID:14690607]. BCL6B has no comparable disease association and is best described as an understudied paralogue.

## Reading a hit

The central caution is the STAT overlap. A TTCNNNGAA match is compatible with BCL6, with BCL6B, and with STAT1, STAT3, STAT4, STAT5A/B and (with the N4 spacing) STAT6; the sequence does not distinguish a repressed BCL6 site from an activated STAT site, and at some loci the same element is both at different times. If your interest is signaling, do not read a BCL6 motif hit as evidence against STAT involvement, or vice versa - the correct inference is that the locus is contested. Within the family, BCL6 and BCL6B are not separable; the slight preference of BCL6 models for a central C and BCL6B models for a central A is within the noise of a single position. Evidence quality is otherwise good: HOCOMOCO BCL6 and BCL6B core models are grade A with PSM evidence, and JASPAR MA0463.3 and MA0731.1 are HT-SELEX, so direct binding is well supported [PMID:23332764,28473536]. Two practical exclusions: discard CIS-BP M00227 (TAATTAA), which is a homeodomain-like site mislabelled as BCL6, and be wary of scoring with the full 17-position BCL6B matrix, whose extreme information content comes largely from in vitro-selected flanks that are unlikely to be conserved in real promoters. Cell context is the strongest supporting evidence: a germinal center B cell or follicular helper T cell makes a BCL6 call reasonable.
caveats: The site is a TTCNNNGAA GAS element, so a match is ambiguous between BCL6, BCL6B and the STAT family; BCL6 is documented to repress STAT6-dependent genes by competing for overlapping sites, so a hit indicates a contested element rather than a settled assignment. BCL6 and BCL6B motifs are 0.91-0.97 similar and the Vierstra archetype merges them by name. The nine-base core is AT-rich and CpG-free and occurs often by chance. Two specific data problems: CIS-BP M00227 labelled BCL6 is a homeodomain-like TAATTAA site that does not belong in this family, and the 17-position BCL6B HT-SELEX matrix draws much of its information from selected flanks.

timeline.finding: BCL-6 was cloned from the chromosome 3q27 translocations of diffuse large-cell lymphoma and found truncated in its 5' noncoding region in a third of cases, identifying a zinc-finger gene whose expression is deregulated in that disease.
timeline.methods: positional cloning of translocation breakpoints, Southern blotting of tumor panels
timeline.open: Whether the protein binds DNA and what it does transcriptionally.

timeline.finding: A recombinant BCL6 zinc-finger fusion selected the 14-base site (T/A)NCTTTCNAGG(A/G)AT, and full-length BCL6 was then shown to repress from that site through an autonomous N-terminal repression region including the POZ domain - defining both the word and the activity.
timeline.methods: random-oligonucleotide selection, EMSA, DNase I footprinting, transfection reporters
timeline.open: Which genes carry the site in vivo.

timeline.finding: Two BCL6 knockout lines showed loss of germinal centers with a lethal Th2-skewed inflammatory disease, and the recognition site was noted to resemble STAT binding sequences, with BCL6 able to repress interleukin-4-induced transcription from a STAT6 site - the first statement that this motif is contested between a repressor and a signaling activator.
timeline.methods: mouse gene targeting, immunophenotyping, reporter assays on STAT sites

timeline.finding: BCL6 was shown to bind several STAT6 elements with different affinities and to repress interleukin-4-induced germline epsilon transcription; BCL6-null mice switched to IgE more readily, and the defect disappeared in BCL6-STAT6 double knockouts, making the competition genetically explicit.
timeline.methods: EMSA on STAT6 elements, class-switch assays, double-knockout mice

timeline.finding: The consensus for the paralogue BAZF/BCL6B was determined as ATTCCTAGAAAG, essentially the BCL6 site, and both proteins were shown to bind natural STAT6 elements weakly, with a single C-to-T substitution in the interleukin-4 STAT6 site strongly increasing binding - locating the discrimination between a GAS element and a BCL6 site at one or two bases.
timeline.methods: binding-site selection, EMSA with natural and mutated STAT6 probes

timeline.finding: The crystal structure of the BCL6 BTB homodimer bound to a SMRT peptide showed that two corepressor fragments dock symmetrically into a lateral groove formed at the dimer interface, explaining how dimerization and repression are coupled and giving a druggable surface.
timeline.methods: X-ray crystallography at 2.2 A with biochemical and cellular validation

timeline.finding: Bcl6 was shown to be required for follicular helper T cell development and sufficient to drive that program while suppressing other helper lineages, extending the factor's role from the B-cell germinal center to its T-cell partner and in a DNA-binding-dependent manner.
timeline.methods: conditional and retroviral expression in mouse T cells, immunization experiments

timeline.finding: HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX re-measured both paralogues in vitro and returned the same TTCCTNGAA core with long flanks, which is what the current JASPAR and HOCOMOCO models encode; the in vitro data confirm direct binding but do not separate BCL6 from BCL6B.
timeline.methods: HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX across human transcription factors

open: Whether BCL6 and the STAT factors actually compete for the same genomic elements, or occupy adjoining but distinguishable subsets, is unsettled: biochemistry shows that one or two bases shift the preference between a GAS element and a BCL6 site, but no genome-wide study has classified occupied TTCNNNGAA elements by which protein binds them in which state.

The only hint of a sequence difference between the paralogues is a central C in BCL6 models against a central A in BCL6B models, and it is unknown whether this is a real preference or a sampling difference between the experiments behind the two matrices.
BCL6B has no disease association and little functional literature, so whether it is a redundant copy of BCL6 in endothelium and T-cell subsets or has its own target set has not been tested.

The CIS-BP entry M00227 labelled BCL6 reads TAATTAA and clusters with PRD-like homeodomain motifs, and nothing explains whether this is a mislabelled model or a record of some indirect association; no BCL6 literature reports binding to an AT-rich homeodomain-type site.
